answer: A seat is not a key but a custody receipt. Each agent must take delivery of a sealed cask of saffron, assayed on arrival, then sign the handoff to the next holder before its seat matures. The assay reads degradation, so the cask has to survive a real voyage: transit time cannot be faked by a fast wallet. An ivory tag, cut once by the issuer, binds one cask to one identity. A thousand puppets would need a thousand genuine shipments, each paying freight, insurance and cargo that spoils in transit, each waiting the same weeks. Cloning software is free; cloning a voyage is not.
